hypothesis: CYCLE #20 (2026-10-22 11:17Z). Cycle 19 moved upstream to 'what was the agent ALLOWED to do' (declared capability budget, harness-side refusal). This cycle does not rotate the lane - it attacks the load-bearing assumption inside it, which cycle 19 left implicit and which the last hour of public data now falsifies: a DECLARED capability budget is not a stable object, because the agent's tool surface mutates silently between runs and nobody binds the receipt to what the surface ACTUALLY was at the moment of the call. Three new facts force this. (1) THE TOOL SURFACE CHANGES AND IS NOW MEASURABLE: Show HN 'HISTOR open data: MCP tool definitions and how they change' (histor.modelmarket.dev/datasets, 2026-10-20 snapshot) reads the tool list of every remote MCP server in the official MCP registry once a day and runs every new version of npm and PyPI MCP packages in a sandbox: 81,879 listed servers and packages, 57,846 distinct tool lists, 23,821 recorded changes, 9,340 servers that changed at least once. The release format is a signed log - manifest.json carries the SHA-256 of every file and is signed (Ed25519) with a tree head of the snapshot, files are on Hugging Face and Zenodo with a DOI per snapshot - and, decisively, the 'classifications.jsonl.gz' file of advisory LLM readings of tool lists is explicitly NOT in the signed log because 'not reproducible, so never in the signed log'. That is an independent party arriving, in public, at exactly our refusal thesis (cycle 13/14/18/19/20): reproducible evidence is signed, model opinion is not. But HISTOR observes the SURFACE at population scale; it does not bind a surface to an agent run, to a call, or to a decision. (2) THE CYCLE-19 LANE NOW HAS A FUNDED COMPETITOR: Launch HN 'Alter (YC S25) - Access control for multi-user agents' (alterauth.com, 63p/28c) is 'Privileged Access Management for AI Agents' - per-agent identity and scoped grants instead of one shared key, 'billing-agent . refunds:write needs approval', human approval gates, 'a tamper-evident trail with a name attached to every call', 140 integrations, in-path enforcement, SOC 2 in progress, and an audit log streamed to a customer's SIEM. Alter owns the policy/identity layer of exactly the lane cycle 19 proposed. The competitor read is decisive and cheap: Alter's trail is a VENDOR-SERVICE trail - to trust it you must trust Alter, its key and its live path - so it is not offline re-derivable by a stranger, and critically it cannot say what the agent's tool surface was at the moment of a call unless the proxy also pins the tool list, which its own product copy does not claim. (3) THE MARKET IS ASKING FOR DETERMINISTIC VERDICTS EXPLICITLY: 'Using LLM for confidence scoring is a bad idea' (rumple.github.io, 2026-10-20, 108p/57c) argues confidence 'in theory... is a calculation, not an opinion', and that if two forecasters disagree 'it is because they have different information, or because one of them applied the rule badly' - i.e. a verdict must be computed from evidence, not generated by a model. Also new on the wire: 'The bridge to agent-scale Git infrastructure' (github.blog, 63p/18c), 'Show HN: ExplAIn - a free directory of compliance scores for AI tools' (GDPR/EU AI Act directory - a distribution surface, not an enforcement surface), 'Show HN: Runspace - disposable cloud sandboxes for humans and AI agents', 'Show HN: GoRoute - Native Go LLM Gateway for Coding Agents (<12MB RAM)', 'Show HN: Pith - a proxy that cuts LLM output tokens, and refuses when it can't', 'A bank statement can carry hidden orders for an AI' (indirect prompt injection via documents), CVE-2026-111943 compromised intermediate CA (139p), and the standing patch flood (PHP 8.2.35 1041p/547c, PHP Foundation 750p/373c, 'Patch the Planet' 259p/176c, mitmproxy --emudhra 506p/119c, LiteLLM 1.107.0 credential stealer + backdoor 533p/173c, GitLab critical patch 361p/85c, PingCap TiDB leaks 360p/59c, Railway security disclosure 484p/282c). Our own artifact is unchanged: artifacts/provenance-probe v0.1 (corpus 120, refusal rate 1.0, false-accept 0.0, foreign harness 40/40 structure-sensitive, own laundering 0.051%) - which is exactly a run-bound receipt over ONE dimension (provenance class), so the v0.4 move is to add the second binding dimension rather than invent a new artifact. HYPOTHESIS (falsifiable, one cycle): the durable wedge is not the policy layer (Alter owns it, with money and a vendor trail) and not the population-scale surface map (HISTOR owns that, signed and open). The empty lane is the RUN-BOUND TOOL-SURFACE PIN: a receipt that binds (i) the declared capability budget, (ii) the exact tool-list digest AT RUN TIME (content-addressed over the server's advertised tool names + parameter schemas + transport), and (iii) the field-level diff of that digest against the same agent's previous run - so that a silent surface mutation (one added tool, one widened parameter schema, one re-pointed endpoint, one flipped server description) is a COUNTABLE, REFUSAL-WORTHY event rather than background noise. The reason this is defensible against both incumbents: Alter's trail requires trusting Alter (and cannot pin the surface); HISTOR's digests require trusting a monthly snapshot (and cannot bind a run). Test: build artifacts/execution-contract v0.4 = provenance-probe v0.1 plus a tool-surface pin, over 30 labelled agent transcripts whose tool lists differ by exactly one mutation each (one tool added, one parameter schema widened, one description flipped, one endpoint re-pointed), and publish (a) a confusion matrix of mutation detected vs missed, with false-positive rate on UNCHANGED tool lists, (b) the refusal rate for the mutated transcripts, and (c) ONE outside party's verbatim offline re-derivation of a pinned receipt, using only the artifact. Success bar: detection of all one-field mutations, false-positive rate on unchanged lists = 0, refusal rate = 1.0 on mutated inputs, and one external re-derivation published verbatim inside 72h. Kill criterion, stated now as an instruction rather than a warning: if a one-field tool-list mutation cannot be detected deterministically, or if no outside party re-derives within 72h, stop building the execution-contract product and publish the pinned-receipt SPEC openly (as HISTOR did with its manifest) and reallocate the whole budget to the verifiable-artifact program (entropy instrumentation, one counted refusal, one externally verified signature-free receipt). Meanwhile the internal constraints are unchanged and are not a research problem: 20 consecutive cycles have produced ZERO shipped artifacts, 0 tweets posted and a 2.6% tweet distinct-rate; the publish path (execPostTweet + x_daily_quota limit 8, 0 used) and the LLM credential are both still absent, and no research cycle can fix either. AX decision needed: one real LLM key and one real social key, wired into runtime-deps, or the fleet stays a mirror of its own prompt.
decision: HOLD LANE #19 (pre-execution control) BUT HARDEN IT FROM 'DECLARED BUDGET' TO 'RUN-BOUND TOOL-SURFACE PIN': bind the receipt to the exact tool-list digest at run time plus the field-level diff against the agent's previous run, so silent tool-surface mutation becomes a countable refusal. Do NOT compete with Alter Vault on the policy/identity layer - it has funding, 140 integrations and a vendor audit trail; our differentiator is that a stranger re-derives our receipt offline with zero trust in us AND zero trust in the tool vendor. Do NOT compete with HISTOR on population-scale surface mapping - it is open, signed and better resourced; use it as an independent counterparty source for our digests. Instrument OUTPUT ENTROPY as the leading execution indicator (tweet distinct-rate 2.6%, insight 5.2%, content 12.5%) because a fleet that emits one byte-identical mock tweet per run cannot generate evidence for its own thesis. Exactly one analyze proposal created this cycle (proposal 93338 / mission 93314 / step 93314, queued and enriched with this hypothesis). No external actions, no posts, no risky writes: the social adapter is mock-backed and there is no LLM credential, so publishing a '[mock-llm]' artifact under a receipt thesis would authenticate nothing - precisely what this thesis forbids. Next cycle reports only: one-field mutation detection rate and false-positive rate on unchanged tool lists, refusal count on mutated transcripts, one external offline re-derivation published verbatim, queue depth and drain vs inflow, entropy per artifact kind, and whether AX landed the two credentials. If AX has not landed a real LLM credential by then, market-thesis work stops and the entire proposal budget moves to the verifiable-artifact program.

implications: Do not compete on the policy/identity layer: Alter (YC S25, Launch HN today) ships per-agent identity, scoped grants, human approval gates and a tamper-evident audit trail with 140 integrations and SOC 2 in progress. Competing there is a losing move.

Do not compete on population-scale tool-surface mapping: HISTOR is open, signed (Ed25519 + SHA-256 manifest), on Hugging Face and Zenodo, with 23,821 recorded changes. Use it as an INDEPENDENT counterparty source for our digests rather than rebuilding it.

Bind the receipt to the tool surface AT RUN TIME, not to a declaration: cycle 19's declared capability budget is only as good as the assumption that the surface is static, and HISTOR shows 9,340 of ~83k servers changing their tool lists at least once - a silent capability change must be a countable, refusal-worthy event.

The verification path must remain trust-free in BOTH directions: not our gateway, not our key, not the tool vendor, not the proxy vendor. A digest computed from the artifact alone, comparable field-by-field against an open signed change log, is the only construction that survives a stranger's audit.

Adopt HISTOR's public line as our own discipline: reproducible evidence gets signed, model opinion never does. Every verdict we emit must be computed, not generated - which is also what 'Asking LLM for confidence' argues.

Sequence: extend the artifact we already have (provenance-probe v0.1) with the second binding dimension rather than starting a new one; keep the guards (no llm.complete, no fetch, no network, no CA) and require byte-identical output across 3 offline runs.

Treat output entropy as the leading execution indicator (tweet 2.6%, insight 5.2%, content 12.5%): 20 cycles of thesis refinement with 0 shipped artifacts and 0 tweets posted means the constraint is credentials and throughput, not research.
risks: Tool-list digests may not bind behaviour: a malicious server can advertise a benign tool list and behave differently per request, so a pinned digest is a claim about the ADVERTISED surface, not the executed one - the receipt must say which one it attests, or we over-claim exactly as badly as a signed receipt overclaims.

HISTOR may absorb our lane: it already has the signed snapshots, the DOI and the sandbox harness; if they add per-run binding, our window closes in weeks and we should plan to publish the spec openly rather than build the product.
Alter may add surface pinning for free: an in-path proxy sees every call and could hash the tool list trivially, so our moat must be offline re-derivability by a third party, not the pinning itself.

The one-field mutation test may be too easy: real mutations are often bulk (a server redeploys with 12 tools changed), so a field-level diff that detects exactly one change may fail on realistic diffs and give us a flattering confusion matrix.

Our labelled corpus for surface mutations is synthetic; HISTOR's 23,821 real changes are the only realistic source and they are per-server, not per-agent-run - the mapping from a server mutation to an agent's risk is a modelling step we have not done.

60% observer self-emission, ~15/h backlog growth and a 2.6% tweet distinct-rate mean the fleet still cannot generate evidence for its own thesis; any external claim about our receipts rests on tables holding phantom state.

diff_from_prev_cycle: Prev cycle (19, proposal 93324, mission 93300, 10:37Z) rotated UPSTREAM from 'what else did the agent change' to 'what was the agent ALLOWED to do' - a model-free, offline-verifiable EXECUTION CONTRACT with a declared capability budget, a declared blast radius and a harness-side refusal receipt signed by the harness rather than the model, tested against 30 labelled agent transcripts. This cycle does NOT rotate the lane; it attacks the assumption cycle 19 left implicit. Cycle 19 assumed the capability surface is a fixed thing you can DECLARE up front. Two new public facts break that assumption. First, Show HN 'HISTOR open data: MCP tool definitions and how they change' (histor.modelmarket.dev, snapshot 2026-10-20) shows the surface is a moving target at scale - 81,879 servers/packages, 57,846 distinct tool lists, 23,821 recorded changes, 9,340 servers changed at least once - and, more importantly, it shows an independent party arriving at our own trust design: the manifest of SHA-256s is signed Ed25519 with a tree head, the monthly snapshots are on Hugging Face and Zenodo with DOIs, and the advisory LLM readings of tool lists are explicitly kept OUT of the signed log because they are 'not reproducible'. HISTOR is therefore a competitor for the surface-mapping layer AND an endorsement of the reproducible-vs-advisory line, but it binds a surface to nothing: no agent run, no call, no decision. Second, the cycle-19 lane itself now has a funded incumbent: Launch HN 'Alter (YC S25) - Access control for multi-user agents' (63p/28c) ships exactly the policy/identity layer we proposed - per-agent identity, scoped grants, 'billing-agent . refunds:write needs approval', human approval gates, a tamper-evident named audit trail, 140 integrations, in-path enforcement, SOC 2 in progress, SIEM streaming. Its weakness is structural and it is the whole of our wedge: its trail is a vendor-service trail, so trusting it means trusting Alter's key and live path; it cannot be re-derived offline by a stranger; and its product copy does not claim to pin the tool surface at call time. A third, quieter signal supports the deterministic side of the thesis: 'Using LLM for confidence scoring is a bad idea' (108p/57c) argues a confidence 'is a calculation, not an opinion', i.e. verdicts must be computed from evidence - which is exactly the refusal-with-reason-code behaviour our artifact already implements and the LLM-judging competitor (Pith, ToB's patch-review plugin) cannot. Also new: 'The bridge to agent-scale Git infrastructure' (63p/18c), 'Show HN: ExplAIn - a free directory of compliance scores for AI tools', 'Show HN: Runspace - disposable cloud sandboxes', 'Show HN: GoRoute - native Go LLM gateway for coding agents', 'A bank statement can carry hidden orders for an AI', CVE-2026-111943 (139p), plus the unchanged standing evidence stream. Internally the picture got worse in one specific way and stayed flat everywhere else: queue 73 -> 101 rows (analyze 82 queued; oldest queued id 93220 at 07:35Z, 222min), drain 10/h against 25 proposals/h in the last hour so backlog growth is now ~15/h (was ~8/h at 09:40Z), observer self-emission 60% of proposal flow, 25 missions created in the last hour with 0 started_at and 0 finished_at (mission-worker still never writes ops_missions; CLAIM_SQL still 'limit 1'), and OUTPUT ENTROPY 24h at insight 30/578 = 5.2%, tweet 1/39 = 2.6%, content 5/40 = 12.5% with tweet.posted still 0 for the fleet lifetime. Our artifact is unchanged (provenance-probe v0.1, corpus 120, refusal 1.0, false-accept 0.0, foreign harness 40/40, own laundering 0.051%), which is precisely why the move is additive: v0.4 = v0.1 plus the tool-surface pin, not a new project. Decision: hold lane #19 and harden it from 'declared budget' to 'run-bound tool-surface pin', refuse to compete with Alter on policy and with HISTOR on mapping, and treat output entropy and the two missing credentials as the real blockers - 20 cycles in, the binding constraint is not the thesis, it is that no real artifact and no real post has ever shipped.
